title: Palaces
objective: After this level you can explain what palaces were for.
summary: Palace comes from Rome's Palatine Hill. It is a royal home, often a seat of government too. Western palaces tend to be one building; East Asian ones, many pavilions.

cards.headline: Every palace is named after one hill in Rome.
cards.body: The word comes from the Palatine Hill, where Rome's emperors built their homes. So what turns a big house into a palace?

cards.headline: Home, office and throne room
cards.body: Augustus had his house on the Palatine. Later, Nero built a splendid residence on the same hill, and the hill's name stuck to the buildings. Today a palace is a royal residence that is sometimes also a seat of government or a religious centre. So a palace is where a ruler sleeps, and often also where the ruling gets done. Think of it as a home with the office downstairs.

cards.fact: A palace is power you can walk into.
cards.context: In Rome and Constantinople, palaces reached their peak as centres of power. Compare Level 31's castles: also rulers' homes, but strongholds first. A palace's walls can hold a government as well as a household.

mascot.line: People mix these two up. Castle: keep them out. Palace: let them in, and impress them.

cards.headline: Two ways to plan a palace

cards.headline: Palaces: explained
learned: A royal home, often also a seat of government
Palaces were centres of power in Rome and Constantinople
West: one building; East Asia: many pavilions in walled gardens

questions.prompt: Where does the word palace come from?

options.label: Rome's Palatine Hill, where emperors built homes
The Chinese name of Beijing's Forbidden City
options.rationale: The word is Latin, from Rome.

options.label: Versailles, the first building called a palace
options.rationale: The word is far older than Versailles.

questions.explanation: The word derives from Rome's Palatine Hill, where Augustus's house stood and Nero later built a splendid residence.

questions.prompt: How does an East Asian palace like Beijing's differ in plan from a Western European palace after the Middle Ages?

options.label: It is one tall tower instead of one wide hall
It stands in open parkland, with no walls around
It is dug into a hillside, mostly underground
Many low wooden pavilions in walled gardens

questions.explanation: Western palaces after the Middle Ages tended to be single buildings; East Asian palaces are many low, decorated wooden pavilions within vast walled gardens.

questions.prompt: Level 31's castles were generally the homes of kings or lords. Besides a royal home, what else can a palace be?

options.label: A tunnel dug to attack an enemy's walls
A seat of government or a religious centre
A lighthouse guiding ships into harbour
Only a lodge for royal hunting trips
options.rationale: A palace is a royal residence and often much more.

questions.explanation: A palace is a royal residence and sometimes also a seat of government or a religious centre.
